text.arabic_uthmani: أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًۭا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًۭا ۚ لَّا يَسْتَوُۥنَ

words.gloss_range: consequential connective opening a rhetorical comparison from the prior reward disclosure
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) opens the comparison as a consequence, not as a loose new topic. After the hidden reward disclosed in 32:17, the ayah turns that prior statement into an equality test: can the believer-state and the transgressor-state be treated alike? In the compact opening complex, the linkage and question-force arrive together, so the reader hears both continuity with the prior ayah and a fresh rhetorical challenge.

topics.headline: consequential rhetorical opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison is argued from the prior reward disclosure in 32:17 rather than introduced as an isolated classification.
topics.reason: The connective relation is licensed, and the interrogative force survives as part of the opening complex; the local word itself is treated as the consequential connector rather than as a separate bare interrogative particle.

topics.headline: boundary pivot into comparison
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 32:18 as the hinge where reward disclosure becomes a test of equivalence.
topics.reason: The boundary rows cohere with the local comparison and with the previous ayah as argumentative ground.

topics.headline: compact challenge form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the opening as compressed and abrupt, with linkage and challenge packed into the first beat.
topics.reason: The sound and compact-form observations are local surface payoffs and do not alter the syntax.

words.gloss_range: open relative person-class forming the first side of the comparison
words.prose: The first {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) opens an unrestricted person-class rather than naming a single individual. Its singular surface licenses the singular copula that follows, but its open relative force lets the final plural verdict later expand the example into a class principle. Because the same pronoun form will return after the comparison marker, the predicates become the real contrast inside a deliberately balanced frame.

topics.headline: open first comparand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first side is any person bearing the believer-state, not a named or closed target.
topics.reason: The first relative pronoun is locally the subject of the first state clause and keeps the referent open.

topics.headline: singular form opens into class verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how a singular-form comparand can become part of the later plural class judgment.
topics.reason: The local singular agreement is clear, and the final plural verb supplies the later semantic expansion.

topics.headline: paired relative frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated relative form that makes the two predicate states stand out as the only decisive difference.
topics.reason: The second relative pronoun is explicitly governed by the comparison marker, so the repeated form supports symmetry without erasing syntactic difference.

words.gloss_range: perfect copula establishing the first comparand's believer-state
words.root_gloss_range: being, occurrence, state, and temporal predication; local grammar selects copular predication, not production or surety branches
words.prose: The first {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) makes the believer predicate a settled state inside the comparison. Its copular frame requires the predicate that follows, so the ayah is not describing an event by this word alone; it is installing a status for the first comparand. The exact finite form will be repeated in the second arm, which keeps the grammatical frame equal while the two predicates carry the opposition. This state-language also joins the local movement from hidden reward in 32:17 to the believers named by completed action in 32:19.

topics.headline: copular state with being pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief is installed as the first comparand's standing state, while broader being and becoming senses remain only lexical pressure.
topics.reason: The local verb instance is copular and takes a predicate; existential or ontological language must be qualified by that syntax.

topics.headline: mirrored state frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that both sides enter through the same copular doorway, so the verdict cannot be blamed on uneven grammar.
topics.reason: The second instance repeats the same form and function, creating a local structural mirror.

topics.headline: local state thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can follow this state-language into the surrounding same-surah movement where the believer class is named again in 32:19.
topics.reason: The same-surah and co-occurrence rows provide provenance for a local thread without creating a new lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative active participle naming the believer-state in the first comparison arm
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, faithfulness, and belief; local Form IV active participle selects believer while retaining trust and safety pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the matched transgressor predicate in the second comparison arm

words.prose: {{ar:مُؤْمِنًا}} ({{tr:muʾminan}}) supplies the first arm's identity: an open believer-state assigned by the preceding copula. Its accusative indefiniteness makes the category available to any qualifying person, not a closed title. The root field keeps belief tied to trust, security, and fidelity, while the local form keeps the selected sense as believer rather than merely someone made safe. Placed opposite {{ar:فَاسِقًا}} ({{tr:fāsiqan}}), it becomes the positive pole of a trust-versus-boundary-exit contrast that 32:19 will immediately resume as accomplished belief. Its inner hamza gives the believer term a small marked catch before the comparison moves onward.

topics.headline: open predicate identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the believer label is a predicate-state open to any qualifying person, not an independent subject or closed title.
topics.reason: The noun instance is an indefinite accusative predicate of the first copula.

topics.headline: trust and security field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees belief as a trust-bearing status with security and fidelity pressure, while local grammar keeps believer as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The root field supports trust and security pressure, but claims about generating safety for others are kept as lexical pressure rather than replacing the ordinary believer sense.

topics.headline: positive pole in lexical antithesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the contrast with the transgressor term is lexical and structural, not merely thematic.
topics.reason: The ayah places the two active participles in matched predicate slots, and the distribution rows support the polarity.

topics.headline: same-surah belief bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the singular category in 32:18 become the plural accomplished believers whose outcome is specified in 32:19.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete same-surah references and preserve the direction from question category to following outcome.

topics.headline: marked inner articulation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the believer term as internally marked before the comparison moves onward.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is modest and local.

words.gloss_range: bound comparison marker governing the second relative clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the compressed comparison marker plus relative pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) is the hinge that turns the first predicate-state into a likeness test. It governs the second {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}), so the second clause is not an appositional restatement but the counter-arm of the comparison. The compact {{ar:كَمَنْ}} ({{tr:ka-man}}) surface makes that second arm enter quickly, and the nasal close of {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) makes the marker and pronoun sound like one tight comparand-opening before the final negation rejects the staged likeness.

topics.headline: comparative governance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second person-class is grammatically governed as the comparison's counter-arm, not merely listed beside the first.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence forces the second relative pronoun under the comparison marker.

topics.headline: likeness staged for rejection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah first stage comparability so the later denial can reject equality precisely.
topics.reason: The comparison marker aligns the two arms before the final answer clause denies leveling.

topics.headline: compact comparand entry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the comparison marker and its pronoun as one tight entry into the second arm.
topics.reason: The bound surface form and local sound observation are valid surface-level payoffs.

words.gloss_range: second open relative person-class governed by the comparison marker

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the comparison marker governing this second relative pronoun

words.prose: The second {{ar:مَنْ}} ({{tr:man}}) repeats the open person-class form, but now under the governance of {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}). That creates a formal mirror with a syntactic difference: the first relative head opens the positive arm, while this one opens the compared counter-arm. Its openness keeps the transgressor predicate generic, so the final verdict applies to any bearer of that state.

topics.headline: governed second comparand
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second relative pronoun is the comparison marker's governed counter-arm, not a duplicate of the first pronoun's syntax.
topics.reason: The attachment data makes the second relative pronoun both governed by the comparison marker and subject of the second copula.

topics.headline: open transgressor class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second predicate as an open class-state rather than a single known opponent.
topics.reason: The same relative form keeps the referent generic.

topics.headline: mirrored relative architecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that repeated relative heads make the two states maximally comparable before the denial breaks the balance.
topics.reason: The two relative clauses are locally parallel, with the second introduced by the comparison marker.

words.gloss_range: second perfect copula establishing the counter-comparand's transgressor-state
words.root_gloss_range: being, occurrence, state, and temporal predication; local grammar selects copular predication, not production or surety branches

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the transgressor predicate required by the second copula

words.prose: The second {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) repeats the same copular frame for the counter-arm. It requires {{ar:فَاسِقًا}} ({{tr:fāsiqan}}) as its predicate and presents that state as settled for the comparison. Because the verb form does not change from the first arm, the ayah removes aspect or grammar as the source of difference; only the opposed predicates remain to be judged by the closing non-equivalence. The state-frame then points forward to 32:20, where the transgressor category becomes a completed plural act.

topics.headline: second copular state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the transgressor term is installed as a standing predicate-state, while broader being language remains bounded by copular syntax.
topics.reason: The local verb is copular and predicate-taking; existential force is qualified rather than made the primary parse.

topics.headline: exact frame reprise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second arm mirror the first so the contrast is fair on the surface before it is denied as equal.
topics.reason: The second copula matches the first in form, position, and copular role.

topics.headline: local outcome bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can follow the state label here into the plural completed transgression described in 32:20.
topics.reason: The same-surah rows give concrete forward provenance and do not override the local copular frame.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative active participle naming the transgressor-state in the second comparison arm
words.root_gloss_range: departure from command, transgression, and boundary-exit imagery; local active participle selects a person-type, not an abstract act

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the matched believer predicate in the first comparison arm

words.prose: {{ar:فَاسِقًا}} ({{tr:fāsiqan}}) completes the second arm as the matched predicate to {{ar:مُؤْمِنًا}} ({{tr:muʾminan}}). Its indefinite accusative form keeps the category open, while the active participle makes the comparison about a person-type rather than an abstract act. The root field brings exit and rupture into the moral label, so the ayah contrasts trust and security with boundary-breakage before the closing verdict denies that the two can be leveled. The same root returns in 32:20 as completed plural transgression, showing the label immediately unpacked by deed-language. Its sibilant movement into a hard qāf closure gives the rupture term a rougher stop just before the smoother leveling verb.

topics.headline: open predicate counterpole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the transgressor term is the second open predicate-state in the same grammatical slot as the believer term.
topics.reason: The word is an indefinite accusative predicate of the second copula.

topics.headline: rupture and exit field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees transgression as boundary-exit and rupture imagery applied to a moral state, while local usage keeps the selected sense as transgressor.
topics.reason: The lexicographic branch supports exit imagery, but the local predicate uses it as moral person-description rather than a literal physical split.

topics.headline: active participle person-type
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah compares embodied person-types, not belief against an abstract offense.
topics.reason: The active participle supports person-type salience; agency claims are kept to the basic Form I transgressor profile.

topics.headline: trust versus rupture antithesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the negative pole as lexically opposed to the believer term through security versus exit, not only through moral evaluation.
topics.reason: The local matched predicate slots and co-occurrence evidence preserve the polarity.

topics.headline: same-surah transgression bridge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the singular state-label in 32:18 become the plural completed act in 32:20.
topics.reason: The rows give concrete same-surah recurrence and preserve a forward relation from label to deed.

topics.headline: rupture sound texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the rougher closure of the transgressor term just before the leveling verb arrives.
topics.reason: The sound observation is local and supports, rather than replaces, the lexical rupture image.

words.gloss_range: declarative negation particle opening the explicit verdict clause
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) turns the balanced question into an explicit verdict. It scopes over the single imperfect equality verb, so the ayah is not issuing a prohibition; it is declaring that the proposed leveling fails. Because the negation stands separately at the front of the closure, the polarity switch is visible before the equality verb names exactly what is denied, and the long open vowel lets the denial land audibly before that final verb.

topics.headline: declarative negation scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final clause is a declarative denial of equality, not a command or diffuse sentence-level negation.
topics.reason: The particle negates the following indicative imperfect verb as the answer clause.

topics.headline: verdict pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from staged comparison to explicit mismeasurement correction.
topics.reason: The final verbal clause states the answer to the comparison, with negation placed first.

topics.headline: audible negation landing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the separate negation land before the final leveling verb.
topics.reason: The separate particle and long vowel provide a local surface payoff without changing the syntax.

words.gloss_range: negated Form VIII imperfect equality verb gathering both compared classes into a plural verdict
words.root_gloss_range: levelness, equality, evenness, and mutual standing on one plane; local Form VIII selects intransitive equality, not making-level or directional branches
words.prose: {{ar:يَسْتَوُونَ}} ({{tr:yastawūna}}) is the final verdict word. The Form VIII imperfect gathers the two singular-form relative comparands into one plural subject and denies that they stand level with each other. Its root field makes the denial more concrete than mere difference: the believer-state and transgressor-state cannot be flattened onto the same plane. The clause also answers the opening question internally, joins the recurring non-equivalence formula attested at 35:19 and 39:9, and prepares the differentiated outcomes in 32:19 and 32:20. Its final long-vowel-plus-n cadence resolves the earlier paired predicate endings into the plural sound of the verdict.

topics.headline: plural declarative verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from singular-form comparands to a plural class verdict that denies continuing equality.
topics.reason: The verb is an indicative imperfect plural whose subject is supplied by the two compared classes.

topics.headline: leveling root denial
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the equality denial as non-leveling: the two classes do not stand on the same plane, while local Form VIII keeps the sense intransitive.
topics.reason: The equality and levelness branches support the image, but the local intransitive Form VIII blocks a caused-leveling reading.

topics.headline: equality axis for the antithesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verb supplies the measuring axis that turns the lexical contrast into a categorical verdict.
topics.reason: The final verb evaluates the two predicate roots by denying their leveling.

topics.headline: question answered by formula
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah answer its own rhetorical question and join a recurring non-equivalence formula, with parallels at 35:19 and 39:9.
topics.reason: The formula rows give concrete references and the local clause functions as the internal answer.

topics.headline: same-surah outcome pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final verdict set up the paired outcomes that immediately follow in 32:19 and 32:20.
topics.reason: The same-surah rows provide concrete forward and backward provenance for the verdict's placement.

topics.headline: final cadence shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the paired predicate cadence resolve into the plural ending of the final verdict.
topics.reason: The sound rows are local and reinforce the move from paired predicates to collective closure.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The parallel مَن كَانَ ... كَمَن كَانَ clauses, their predicates مُؤْمِنًا and فَاسِقًا, and the plural negation لَا يَسْتَوُونَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: Two instantiated conditions are compared: settled trust against emergence beyond a containing boundary. Negated equality makes their internal operations non-commensurate, not merely their labels different.

activation_trace.role: Occurrence and presence in time make both kāna frames inhabited conditions rather than bare labels.
Settled security and trust supply the believer's inwardly held configuration.
The date leaving its peel supplies a concrete image of breaching a holding boundary.
Equality and equivalence are explicitly negated, turning the two configurations into unlike operations.

changed_reading.before: A believer and a transgressor are simply two morally unequal kinds of person.
changed_reading.after: The verse contrasts two lived configurations: trust settled within a holding relation and a subject emerging beyond its proper boundary; they do not operate on one scale.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled كَانَ frames each predicate as a condition, while لَا يَسْتَوُونَ closes the comparison.
baseline_models.mechanism: Place or standing from ك و ن combines with formation and just level from س و ي. The denial can therefore concern equal station and integrated formation as well as abstract equality.

activation_trace.role: Place and standing give each predicate a position that can be compared.
Heart-settling assent supplies coherence to one position.
Peel-exit supplies loss of containing form to the opposed position.
Straightness and completion make denied equality also a denial of equal formed integrity.
The level, just midpoint supplies the image of a common plane that the pair does not share.

changed_reading.before: The final verb only says that the two receive different evaluations.
changed_reading.after: The final verb can deny a shared level of station and formed integrity: one condition holds together, while the other has breached its form.

context_deltas.mechanism: Earlier uses distribute س و ي across settling on a locus and fashioning to completion. When the root returns in the focus as denied equality, it carries a latent double resonance of station and formed integrity.

activation_trace.role: Equality is the immediate focus sense whose scope is being revised.
Rising and settling upon a locus adds a station dimension to the later comparison.
Fashioning to straight completion adds formed integrity to what can fail to be equal.

structural_cues: The same root progresses from throne-settlement in 32:4, through human fashioning in 32:9, to negated plural comparison in 32:18.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated root and its distinct branch images; I infer that the earlier station and formation uses remain audible in the focus. The live alternative is that 32:18 activates only ordinary equivalence.

changed_reading.before: They are not equal in value.
changed_reading.after: They neither arrive at the same station nor exhibit the same formed wholeness; moral non-equivalence is rendered as unequal settlement and integration.

context_deltas.mechanism: The believer is not a sealed, motionless inside. Belief answers reminder by falling, the sides break adhesion to beds, and wealth leaves in expenditure, yet this directed relinquishment ends in an embracing refuge. The contrast shifts from inside versus outside to faithful versus misdirected boundary crossing.

activation_trace.role: Settled trust names the relation that remains secure while other attachments are released.
Peel-exit supplies the boundary breach that initially looked like movement itself was blameworthy.
Assent that settles the heart is immediately rendered as responsive action rather than static enclosure.
Sounding downward fall gives belief a forceful movement toward submission.
Breaking adhesion makes departure from the bed a faithful, selective exit.
Wealth going out turns controlled outward flow into a mark of belief.
Joining a gathering refuge supplies the destination that gives the believer's departures their direction.

structural_cues: Ayat 32:15-16 unpack belief into bodily and material movements, and 32:19 gives those movements a gathering destination immediately after the focus.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fall, broken adhesion, outgoing wealth, and refuge; I infer that relation and destination, not motion across a boundary by itself, distinguish faith from fisq. The alternative is that these are independent virtues with no pressure on the peel image.

changed_reading.before: The believer remains safely inside, whereas the fāsiq exits.
changed_reading.after: The believer is selectively permeable: body and wealth leave lesser attachments while trust remains oriented toward refuge. Fisq is not movement itself but a breach that loses the governing relation.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated kāna plus ongoing deeds and certainty turns the focus predicates into compressed biographies. The two persons are unequal as histories of response that have become conditions, not as unexplained essences.

activation_trace.role: Temporal occurrence lets each focus predicate condense a sustained way of being.
Past and continuing presence binds consequence to what the addressees had been doing.
Temporal being links hidden recompense to an enacted history.
Intentional action supplies the repeated conduct sedimented into the focus condition.
The recurring temporal frame carries the believer's outcome back to sustained action.
Deliberate deeds unpack belief into a trajectory rather than a title.
The same temporal frame binds the opposed outcome to sustained denial.
Continued being frames certainty as an enduring practice.
Fixed knowledge supplies the stabilized epistemic habit into which belief can mature.

structural_cues: Forms of بِمَا كُنتُمْ or كَانُوا with ongoing verbs surround 32:18, while 32:24 repeats كَانُوا with certainty.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies temporal recurrence and action clauses; I infer that 32:18 names trajectories after they have acquired continuity. The alternative is that kāna remains a semantically light copula in every occurrence.

changed_reading.before: Believer and fāsiq are fixed identity labels presented without a history.
changed_reading.after: Each label is a temporal achievement: repeated response, action, and denial have become a durable manner of being, so the two histories cannot be leveled.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adjacent outcomes give both groups a maʾwā, but with opposite boundary logics. Believers receive prepared lodging; the peel-exiters seek another exit and are repeatedly returned. Chosen breach becomes involuntary enclosure.

activation_trace.role: Leaving the peel establishes the initial outward motion that the later sequence reverses.
Denied equivalence governs the opposed destination mechanics.
Joining a sheltering collective makes the believer's destination receptive refuge.
Prepared guest provision makes that refuge hospitable rather than coercive.
The focus peel-exit image is repeated at the head of the punitive sequence.
The same gathering-place branch creates a formally parallel but functionally opposite abode.
Passage to the outside repeats the fāsiq's boundary logic as an attempted escape.
Return after departure closes every attempted exit into a punitive loop.

structural_cues: The parallel أَمَّا clauses of 32:19-20 unpack the focus pair; both name a maʾwā, but only 32:20 repeats exit and return.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies peel-exit, parallel abodes, attempted خروج, and forced return; I infer an ironic reversal from self-directed breach to compelled re-enclosure. The alternative is that the shared spatial vocabulary carries no retrospective force into فاسق.

changed_reading.before: The two groups merely receive different destinations.
changed_reading.after: Their non-equality appears as opposed enclosure: faithful relinquishment arrives at welcomed shelter, while boundary breach culminates in an abode where every further exit is reversed.

context_deltas.mechanism: Negated equality becomes a latent partition. The later act of separating between parties and adjudicating divergent paths turns the focus comparison from an opinion about rank into a boundary awaiting public realization.

activation_trace.role: Denied equivalence supplies the distinction that later judgment makes explicit.
Making a boundary visible converts moral difference into separation.
Judgment that distinguishes true from false supplies the legal operation behind the partition.
Separation between parties spatializes the focus denial of a common level.
Taking different paths supplies the divergence on which separation acts.

structural_cues: Ayah 32:25 repeats a plural relation with يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ after 32:18 has denied that the two plurals become equal.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-equivalence, separation, and divergent paths; I infer that judgment actualizes the focus distinction. The alternative is that 32:25 concerns disputed propositions without specifically unfolding the focus pair.

changed_reading.before: The focus offers a rhetorical moral comparison.
changed_reading.after: The focus anticipates a verdict: an already real non-equivalence will be made into a visible boundary between trajectories.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later ecological chain drives water into cut-off earth and brings crop out. Because emergence from concealment can be life-producing, the peel image cannot make every crossing of a boundary inherently corrupt; relation, supply, and fruit distinguish خروج from fisq.

activation_trace.role: Peel-exit is the focus image whose ethical scope the ecological sequence constrains.
Driving and conducting give the water's movement a directing agency.
Conveying water supplies the sustaining input that makes later emergence fruitful.
Earth stripped of vegetation supplies the closed, lifeless starting condition.
Bringing a hidden thing into appearance makes outward emergence explicitly generative.
Growth and cultivation supply the nourishing result by which this exit is judged.

structural_cues: Ayah 32:27 gives a causal material sequence: water is driven to barren land, crop is brought out, and living beings eat.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two outward images with opposite results; I infer that the fāsiq's fault is misrelated exit rather than exteriorization as such. The live alternative is that ف س ق and خ ر ج remain too lexically distant for this material correction to carry much weight.

changed_reading.before: The peel image implies that leaving containment is intrinsically the problem.
changed_reading.after: The verse's boundary image is ethically directional: emergence can nourish when conducted by a sustaining relation, so fisq is a sterile or disloyal breach, not mere outward movement.

context_deltas.mechanism: The final opening admits no benefit from newly presented faith and no reprieve. This activates the temporal branch of the doubled kāna: the focus compares conditions formed within the open interval, not interchangeable declarations made after disclosure closes it.

activation_trace.role: Occurrence in time makes when the predicate becomes true materially relevant.
Heart-settling assent is the condition whose timing the later ayah tests.
Temporal being in the challenge prepares the question of whether a claim has already become a condition.
Decisive opening by judgment marks the closure point after which statuses cannot be exchanged.
The explicit absence of benefit denies efficacy to faith presented only at that point.
Assent appears after disclosure as a declaration that no longer produces the focus condition.
Withholding reprieve removes any further interval in which that assent could become lived trust.

structural_cues: The 32:28 challenge is answered by a day of opening in 32:29, where faith does not benefit and no waiting is granted.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies temporal kāna, decisive opening, non-benefit, and no reprieve; I infer that duration before disclosure helps constitute مَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًا. The alternative is that coercion or sincerity, rather than timing, explains the later faith's failure.

changed_reading.before: Any occurrence of assent could place a person in the believer side of the comparison.
changed_reading.after: The believer is one whose assent became a lived condition while response remained open; post-disclosure assent cannot retroactively make the two trajectories equal.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the packet's split mapping from م ر ي to م و ر supplies oscillation through a form-distant branch. It remains anchored in the focus's settled ء م ن and formed س و ي, reinforced by 32:23-24's doubt-to-certainty sequence. Downstream prose should call it a latent branch resonance, not derive فاسق lexically from doubt or wave motion.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The settled-heart branch of مُؤْمِنًا and the completion branch of لَا يَسْتَوُونَ.

activation_trace.role: Heart at rest supplies the stable pole of the exploratory contrast.
Straight completion supplies the level that oscillation fails to hold.
Doubt and hesitation provide the explicit unstable epistemic state.
The non-dominant wavering branch materializes hesitation as oscillation.
Fixed knowledge supplies the stabilized state reached through enduring response.

changed_reading.before: The focus distinguishes belief from transgression only as moral categories.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also denies equal stabilization: settled trust can hold a formed level, whereas an oscillating epistemic condition cannot.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This reading uses the rare ك و ن surety branch and is therefore more form-distant than ordinary kāna syntax. It remains anchored by the focus's trust and peel-exit images and gains context support from an appointed keeper in 32:11. Downstream prose should present custodianship as an associative activation, not as the verb's direct grammatical meaning.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The doubled كَانَ together with trust-bearing مُؤْمِنًا and boundary-leaving فَاسِقًا.

activation_trace.role: Standing surety or taking charge makes being an exploratory custodial stance.
Security, trust, and what is entrusted supply the charge that can be faithfully held.
Leaving a peel images escape from the boundary that held the charge.
An agent standing over an assigned matter supplies a contextual model of custodial responsibility.

changed_reading.before: The pair names belief and transgression as private states.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the pair contrasts keeping faith with an entrusted charge against slipping the custody and boundary that made trust possible.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates س و ي as other or substitute and ق ر ن as an equal peer while their surface forms bear more ordinary senses. It remains anchored in the focus's كَمَن comparison and denied equality, with later separation supporting non-exchangeability. Downstream prose should frame it as anti-substitution resonance, not a replacement translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The construction أَفَمَن ... كَمَن ... لَا يَسْتَوُونَ asks whether one person can be paired with the other.

activation_trace.role: Otherness and substitution turn denied equality into refusal of interchangeability.
Two actually instantiated conditions prevent the comparison from remaining abstract.
Visible separation supplies the operation that keeps the two conditions from substituting for one another.
The equal-peer branch sharpens the question of who can count as a true counterpart despite shared generation or habitat.

changed_reading.before: The verse says one class scores lower than another on a shared scale.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it refuses substitution: shared humanity, period, or habitat cannot make the two enacted conditions valid counterparts.

strongest_changes: The believer became selectively permeable rather than merely enclosed: body and wealth leave lesser attachments while trust retains direction.
The fāsiq's peel-exit was reversed in 32:20 into attempted exit followed by forced return, producing opposed forms of enclosure.
Repeated س و ي and ك و ن expanded equality into formation, station, enacted history, and time-sensitive commitment.
The generative خروج of crop from barren land prevented the branch image from treating every outward movement as fisq.
summary.what_was_special: The context repeatedly changed a static good-inside versus bad-outside contrast. Faith itself moves, releases, and receives shelter; fisq becomes misrelated breach whose apparent freedom closes into a return loop. Split-root and form-distant activations were retained with explicit containment rather than flattened away.
remaining_uncertainties: How strongly the settlement and completion branches of س و ي remain active under the ordinary equality syntax of 32:18.
Whether the ecological خروج sequence truly qualifies the ف س ق peel image or only offers a useful cross-domain analogy.
The م ر ي to م و ر oscillation, ك و ن surety, and anti-substitution readings are deliberately exploratory and should not be rendered as direct lexical claims.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The two designations encode opposed relations to a containing order.** `ء م ن:B001` supplies settled security and trust, reinforced by trusting assent in `ء م ن:B002`; the packet's sole branch for `ف س ق:B002` is a fresh date emerging from its peel. The balanced *man kāna ... ka-man kāna* puts the figures in formal parallel before denying equivalence. **Inferred arrow:** trusting settlement within the sign-governed relation versus emergence from its containing boundary -> divergent moral trajectories. *Fāsiq* becomes an image of breached containment, not merely a label.

2. **The negation rejects outcome-level interchangeability, not common creaturehood.** `س و ي:B001` is equality, equivalence, and balance. The repeated *kāna* and matched indefinite predicates make the comparison maximally symmetrical, then *lā yastawūn* breaks only the proposed equivalence. **Inferred arrow:** comparable grammatical form does not entail equal operative state. The verse sharpens judgment by first granting a fair comparison frame and then identifying the decisive difference.

3. **The denied equality is tested by the two gathering places that follow.** `س و ي:B001` anchors the fixed negation; in 32:19 and 32:20, both groups receive a *maʾwā* from `ء و ي:B001`, a place toward which one is gathered or sheltered. The packet supplies the repeated shelter word and opposite destinations. **Inferred arrow:** different present relations to trust and boundary -> different terminal gathering points. The next two ayat spatialize the inequality asserted here rather than leaving it abstract.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 32:19-20 supplied the promised spatial proof: both groups receive a *maʾwā* from `ء و ي:B001`, but one gathers into garden-hospitality and the other into burning enclosure. That exact lexical symmetry made 32:18's “not equal” far more concrete than a general evaluative contrast.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak anlatımı, bir şeyin gerçekleşip bulunur hale gelmesini çekirdek kabul eder ve buna olma adları ile geçmiş ya da şimdiki bildirme kullanımlarını bağlar. Pekiştirme, ayırma ve ettirgen oluşturma kullanımları aynı dal içinde bağımlı kullanımlar olarak durur; yer, konum ve üstlenme dalları bu çekirdeğin yerine geçirilmez.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, gerçekleşme ve bulunma çekirdeğiyle sınırlıdır; yer, konum, üstlenme ve boyun eğme ayrı dallardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam hem yalın hem bağlı kullanımlar verdiği için tanım çekirdeği ayrı, bağlı sözleri ayrı tutar.

concept_map.definition: Bu dal, bir şeyin gerçekleşip bulunur hale gelmesini ve bu olmanın geçmiş ya da şimdiki anda bildirilmesini anlatır. Olma adları, pekiştirme ya da ayırma işlevli bağlı sözler ve bir şeyi oldurup oluşmasını sağlama buna bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin gerçekleşmesi, ortaya çıkması ve bulunur halde olması çekirdektir.
Olma ve oluş adları bu çekirdeğin adlaştırılmış biçimleridir.
Geçmişteki bir durumun haber verilmesi veya şimdiki olmanın bildirilmesi bu alana bağlıdır.
Pekiştirme ve gelen kişiyi kapsam dışı bırakma gibi bağlı söz dizimleri çekirdeğe ek kullanımlardır.
Bir şeyi oldurmak, onun gerçekleşmesini sağlama yönünde ettirgen bir uzantıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, dalı bir şeyin olması, gerçekleşmesi ve hazır bulunması etrafında toplar. Aynı bildirim içinde olma adları, geçmiş ya da şimdiki haber verme, pekiştirme, ayırma ve ettirgen oldurma kullanımları da bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

concept_map.definition: Korkunun kalkmasiyla kalbin yatismasi, birine guven verilmesi veya bir kimsenin ya da seyin guvenilir kabul edilmesidir. Bu alan guvenli yer, emanet edilen sey, kendisine guvenilen kisi ve dayanilir binek gibi bagimli uygulamalari da kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek korkuya karsi guven, ic yatiskinligi ve tehlikeden emin olma halidir.
Guven verme, birini kendi koruma ve teminat alani icine alma olarak kullanilir.
Guvenilirlik, ihanete karsi sadakat, emanet edilen sey ve kendisine guvenilen kisi anlamlarini dogurur.
Guvenin bulundugu yer, bir kimsenin emniyet icinde oldugu mesken veya siginak olarak adlandirilir.
Dayanikli ve aksamasindan korkulmayan deve kullanimi, guvenilirlik niteligini canli bir ornege uygular.

branches.source_phrase_ar: أسوى فلان حرفا من كتاب الله أي أسقط وأغفل (ayn)؛ أسويت الشيء أي تركته وأغفلته (sihah)؛ أسوى برزخا ثم رجع إليه (tahdhib)؛ أسوى يعني أسقط وأغفل (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak anlatımı bu gece adını ayın on üçüncü gecesi olarak belirler ve adlandırmayı ayın o sıradaki dengeli görünümüne bağlar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnız ayın on üçüncü gecesinin adıdır; yer ortası, yansızlık ya da genel ay ışığı anlamı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım gece adını kendi başına verir ve başka dallardaki orta, eşitlik veya düzgünlük anlamlarını ona taşımaz.

concept_map.definition: Ayın görünümünün dengelendiği kabul edilen, ayın on üçüncü gecesine verilen ad.

facets.statement: Adlandırılan zaman ayın on üçüncü gecesidir.
Gece adı, ayın o sırada dengeli bir görünüme erişmesi açıklamasıyla ilişkilendirilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar ayın on üçüncü gecesini aynı adla belirler; bunlardan biri adın ayın o gecedeki dengeli görünümüne dayandığını ayrıca açıklar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Ayın dengeli göründüğü kabul edilen belirli geceyi takvim içindeki sırasıyla adlandırmak için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Ayı, geceyi ve ay içindeki on üçüncü sıra koşulunu eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Gece adının hem takvimdeki sırası hem de ayın görünümüyle bağı açıklanmak istendiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: On üçüncü geceyi ve adlandırmanın ayın dengeli görünümüyle kurulan bağını korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: ayın dengeli göründüğü on üçüncü gece

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal ay içindeki belirli bir sıraya, on üçüncü geceye verilen addır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal gökteki ayı, onun ışığını ve ay ışığıyla aydınlanan geceleri genel olarak anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal ayın gece göğündeki görünümü ve aydınlığı çevresindeki aynı zaman alanına bağlıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal yalnız takvimde belirli bir geceyi adlandırır; komşu dal ise ayın kendisini, ışığını ve aydınlattığı geceleri tarih sırasından bağımsız biçimde kapsar.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; seçilen komşu aynı gök ve gece alanını paylaşır, ancak belirli gece adıyla genel ay ve ışık anlamını açıkça ayırır.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه ليلة السواء، وهي ليلة ثلاث عشرة عند استواء القمر في النقلين.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو السواء بمعنى العدل أو الوسط في المكان.
branches.source_phrase_ar: ليلة السواء ليلة ثلاث عشرة (sihah)؛ السواء ممدود ليلة ثلاث عشرة وفيها يستوي القمر (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak anlatımı sabit söz içinde bir kişinin başına denk sayılan mal miktarını verir, fakat aynı kalıp bolluk veya iyi yaşam durumu için de kullanılır; tanım iki görünümü ayırmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnız baş ölçüsü çevresinde kurulan söz kalıbına bağlıdır; genel eşitlik, para adı ya da herhangi bir mal miktarı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız baş ölçüsünü kullanan kalıba bağlanır ve buradaki mal ile bolluk anlamını yalın biçime genellemez.

concept_map.definition: Belirli söz kalıbında bir kişinin başına denk ya da onu karşılar sayılan mal miktarı; aynı kalıpta kişinin içinde bulunduğu bolluk ve iyi yaşam durumu.

facets.statement: Mal miktarı kişinin başına denk sayılan bir ölçüyle anlatılır.
Baş ölçüsüne denk mal düşüncesi, kişinin bolluk ve iyi yaşam içinde bulunmasını anlatmaya genişler.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynak anlatımı başa denk sayılan mal ölçüsü ile bu ölçünün bolluk ve iyi yaşam durumu bildiren kullanımını aynı söz kalıbında birleştirir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnız baş ölçüsü çevresinde kurulan kalıp içinde mal miktarını veya kişinin bolluk içindeki durumunu anlatır.

error_profile.preserves: Başla kurulan denkliği, mal miktarını ve bolluk durumuna uzanan kullanımı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kalıbın bir kişinin başına denk sayılan mal miktarını bildirdiği bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin başını ölçü alan denkliği ve bunun mal miktarı oluşunu korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Aynı söz kalıbının mal ölçüsünden çok kişinin iyi ve bol durumunu anlattığı bağlamda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kalıbın kişiye bağlanan bolluk ve iyi yaşam durumunu korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: başına denk sayılan mal miktarı ya da bolluk

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal baş ölçüsüne bağlı sabit söz içinde mal miktarını ve bolluk durumunu anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal iki şey arasındaki genel ölçü, değer, nicelik veya nitelik denkliğini ve eşlik kalıplarını kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da bir miktarın seçilen ölçüyü karşılaması ve ona denk sayılması ilişkisi vardır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal genel ve üretken denklik alanıdır; odak dal ise yalnız başı ölçü alan kalıpla mal ve bolluk anlatan özel bir kullanımdır.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adayların tamamı değerlendirildi; kökün genel denklik dalı ölçü ilişkisini açıklar ve bu dalın yalnız belirli söz kalıbına bağlı olduğunu gösterir.
branches.branch_image_ar: سِيّ الرأس وقدر يوازي الرأس من مال أو نعمة
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قولهم بسِيّ رأسه أو في سواء رأسه لما يوازي رأسه من مال أو نعمة.
branches.what_is_not_ar: ليس هو السِيّ بمعنى الفضاء، ولا السِيّ بمعنى المثل المطلق، ولا سواء الشيء بمعنى وسطه.
branches.source_phrase_ar: جاء فلان بسِيّ رأسه من المال أي ما يوازي رأسه (jamhara)؛ وقع فلان في سواء رأسه أي فيما ساوى رأسه من النعمة (tahdhib)؛ هو في سِيّ رأسه وسواء رأسه وهي النعمة (tahdhib)
